findings.title: Cleanup service ticker interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: In `CleanUpService.Run`, the ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. This appears to be leftover debugging code and will cause all background cleanup jobs (annotations, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, temp files, user invites, short URLs, and query history) to run every minute instead of every 10 minutes, which also conflicts with the 9-minute job timeout in `clean()`.

findings.title: Leftover Error-level debug logs in annotation cleanup loop spam error logs with ID slices
findings.body: `CleanAnnotations` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 576, 579) call `r.log.Error` before and after every batch even when `err` is `nil` and when no rows are matched. Because these run on every cleanup cycle for each annotation type and for every batch, they will continuously emit false error logs in production and dump entire `ids` slices (up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` elements per batch) into the logs.

findings.title: Quadratic string concatenation when building SQLite DELETE IN clause
findings.body: In `deleteByIDs`, when running on SQLite with `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`, the `IN` list is constructed with `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` inside a loop over `ids`. This performs O(N^2) allocations and memory copies; for a batch of 32,767 IDs (as in the integration test), this allocates and copies several gigabytes of strings per batch. Use `strings.Builder` or `strconv.AppendInt` (as in `getAccessControlFilter` on line 387) to build the clause in O(N) time.
